title: The effects of curcumin supplementation on biomarkers of inflammation, oxidative stress, and endothelial function: A meta-analysis of meta-analyses - ScienceDirect

Thus, this study was conducted to investigate the effects of curcumin supplementation on inflammation, oxidative stress, and endothelial function biomarkers. A meta-analyses of randomized clinical trials was performed by searching PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science up to March 31, 2024.
It has been revealed that curcumin has beneficial properties such as anti-diabetes, antimicrobial, antioxidant, and anti-inflammatory properties [11], [12]. In addition, curcumin inhibits inflammatory cell proliferation and angiogenesis due to its ability to interact with various molecular targets. The regulation of proinflammatory molecules, nitric oxide synthase (NOS) enzymes, cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2), lipoxygenase, and malondialdehyde (MDA) reduction are linked to these properties [9], [13], [14]. However, high heterogeneity exists among the meta-analyses of randomized clinical trials (RCTs) on the influence curcumin supplementation has on oxidative stress and inflammatory and endothelial function biomarkers.
Inflammation is a response to infection and tissue injury by the immune system, which is both biological and physiologic [1]. Chronic inflammation and reduction of anti-oxidant capacity can cause oxidative stress, which increases reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels, causing damage to cell structure [2]. Oxidative stress is related to inflammation, and both can easily cause each other [3], [4], [5]. Inflammation and oxidative stress are both associated with the development of non-communicable diseases like diabetes mellitus (DM), obesity, metabolic syndrome, and different types of cancers [6],
To determine the impact of curcumin supplementation on these indices, the current umbrella meta-analysis included existing systematic reviews and meta-analyses. A thorough systematic search was conducted using databases Embase, PubMed, WOS, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library to acquire peer-reviewed literature published before January 2024. The random-effects model was employed to conduct a meta-analysis.
